Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Travel & transport

identity card noun

also ID card, ID, identification, identity document, ID document

modern

Levi–Bini p. 14

scida persōnae

noun phrase: scida, scidae f., with the genitive persōnae

an identity card

Levi and Bini’s phrase; Traupman and Morgan–Owens have none. Scida (scheda) is classically a strip of papyrus or a sheet of paper (Lewis & Short). The Romans carried no identity papers; the nearest thing was the tessera hospitālis, the token whose matching halves let guest-friends know each other (Plautus, Poenulus; Lewis & Short, s.v. tessera).

Examples

  • Scidam persōnae portitōrī ostende.

    Show your identity card to the customs officer.composed

Other words

  • scida cīvīlis — an identity card

    noun phrase: scida with the adjective cīvīlis · also used · modern · Levi–Bini p. 14

  • scida cīvica — an identity card

    noun phrase: scida with the adjective cīvica · also used · modern · Levi–Bini p. 14

See also passport, driving licence, form, citizen.

SourcesLewis & Short: scida · Lewis & Short: persona · Lewis & Short: civilis · Lewis & Short: civicus · Lewis & Short: tessera

Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 14, s.v. carta. Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no word for an identity card (searched under identity, identification, card and ID).
